content.value_statement: Generic data asset training often misses the needs of different business roles. This skill creates structured courses, exercises, assessments, and delivery plans.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses learner roles, training goals, maturity, budget, schedule, and delivery constraints.
Maps management, finance, data, and business audiences to suitable course modules.
Creates course outlines, lesson schedules, presentation plans, and role-specific learning objectives.
Designs anonymized cases, simulation exercises, question banks, scoring rules, and completion criteria.
Compares internal training, public courses, and public lectures with clear delivery and pricing assumptions.
Drafts completion reports covering attendance, satisfaction, mastery, and recommended next steps.
limitations: It cannot access referenced internal presentations, videos, spreadsheets, or PDFs unless the user provides them.
Its training guidance does not replace accounting, legal, valuation, audit, or financing advice.
Policy citations and pricing references require verification before external or commercial use.
It prepares training materials but cannot deliver live instruction, issue certificates, or measure real learner performance.

use_cases.title: Plan Executive Awareness Training
use_cases.description: Create a concise program covering policy direction, strategic value, investment decisions, and governance responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Build Finance Team Practice
use_cases.description: Develop an accounting-focused course with anonymized cases, simulations, assessments, and clear professional-service boundaries.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Public Data Lecture
use_cases.description: Structure a short public session with audience goals, content modules, interaction, compliance limits, and follow-up options.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Course Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-minute introduction to data assets for [audience]. Include objectives, modules, timing, one case, and a short knowledge check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a focused awareness session.

prompt_templates.title: Design Role-Based Learning Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Design separate learning paths for management, finance, data, and business teams. Show objectives, modules, duration, activities, and expected outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a program for several enterprise roles.

prompt_templates.title: Develop an Applied Workshop
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [duration] workshop for [role] on [topic]. Include anonymized cases, simulation tasks, scoring criteria, assessment questions, and facilitator notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn course content into practical exercises.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Complete Training Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these requirements: [details], produce a diagnostic summary, curriculum, schedule, materials list, assessment plan, delivery risks, pricing assumptions, and evaluation framework.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare an advanced proposal for stakeholder approval.

output_examples.input: Plan a half-day data asset session for senior managers.
output: Objective: enable informed decisions on data asset investment and governance.
Agenda: policy context, value pathways, governance roles, decision case, and action planning.
Assessment: a short scenario discussion and executive action checklist.

output_examples.input: Create an assessment plan for a finance team workshop.
output: Use policy questions, accounting judgment scenarios, and one anonymized classification exercise.
Set transparent scoring criteria and explain that passing does not qualify participants for professional practice.
Report group mastery, common errors, and recommended follow-up support.

output_examples.input: Compare internal training with a public lecture.
output_examples.output: Internal training supports deeper practice and custom cases. A public lecture provides broad awareness with limited exercises, assessment, and personalization.

best_practices: Define learner roles and measurable outcomes before selecting modules or materials.
Use anonymized or fictional cases and confirm permissions for every external training asset.
Verify current policies, pricing assumptions, and professional boundaries before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not teach every role with one undifferentiated agenda.
Do not promise accounting recognition, financing, certification, or other regulated outcomes.
Do not use confidential business data, copyrighted materials, or unverified policy claims.

faq.question: Which audiences does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports management, finance, data, business, and general industry audiences through separate learning paths.

faq.question: Can it create complete presentation files?
faq.answer: It can draft slide structures and content. Final branded files require templates, source materials, and production tools.

faq.question: Can it use our company data in exercises?
faq.answer: Use only approved, anonymized data. Prefer fictional cases when confidentiality, consent, or data handling controls are unclear.

faq.question: Does the training replace professional advice?
faq.answer: No. Accounting, legal, audit, valuation, and financing decisions require qualified professionals and organization-specific evidence.

faq.question: How should policy references be handled?
faq.answer: Verify every policy title, identifier, effective date, and interpretation against current authoritative sources before delivery.

faq.question: What information improves the training plan?
faq.answer: Provide audience roles, current maturity, learning goals, available time, delivery format, budget, source materials, and assessment expectations.
